articles.title: Fed’s Goolsbee calls CPI ‘borderline disturbing’, flags three inflation worries
articles.expand: Strong language like this from Goolsbee adds weight to the hawkish run of Fed commentary after the CPI report, and it strengthens pricing for a December hike. His focus on services and expectations points to concern about entrenched inflation, not transitory shocks, which raises the risk of a longer hiking cycle. That backdrop supports the US dollar and front-end Treasury yields, and remains a headwind for gold. With energy feeding the cost side of inflation, oil prices stay central to how hawkish the Fed may need to be. --- Earlier: Fed’s Paulson backs further gradual rate hikes, names three ...

articles.title: Fed’s Paulson backs further gradual rate hikes, names three triggers for faster action
articles.expand: Paulson’s comments add a voting member’s voice to the hawkish chorus after the hot CPI report, which reinforces pricing for a December hike and a follow-up in January. Her emphasis on gradual steps tempers the case for a half-point move, but her three triggers for faster action leave that door open if data keeps running hot. That combination supports the US dollar and front-end Treasury yields, while a firmer hiking path remains a headwind for gold. Because she names energy prices as an inflation driver, any further Middle East-driven gains in oil now feed directly into the Fed’s tightening ca...
